summary: Supplementaries crashed the game while it was starting, because its library mod Moonlight Lib hadn't finished setting up its villager-trade code (ModItemListing.CODEC was null).
root_quote: Caused by: java.lang.NullPointerException: Cannot invoke "com.mojang.serialization.Codec.fieldOf(String)" because "net.mehvahdjukaar.moonlight.api.trades.ModItemListing.CODEC" is null
note: This is a player's game (client) crash, not a server crash: it says Type: Client on line 48. The last Caused by line points into Moonlight Lib, called from Supplementaries. Likely fix: update both mods to versions made for each other. I found no public bug report for this exact error.

summary: The server's watchdog shut it down while it was still starting up (Forge was loading every mod's language files), because start-up ran past the max-tick-time limit.
root_quote: java.lang.Error: ServerHangWatchdog detected that a single server tick took 0.00 seconds (should be max 0.05)
note: No Caused by line and no mod in the stack: line 6 is Forge's own start-up code and 0 players were online (line 694). The log shows a slow start-up, not which mod made it slow. Usual fix: set max-tick-time=-1 in server.properties while testing, then trim heavy mods or use a faster host.

summary: A quest villager from the Quest Giver mod crashed the server while looking for a path to a work block, because two different target spots were treated as the same point.

note: The error happens inside vanilla pathfinding code, and several mods change villager AI here (Radium, Liberty's Villagers, Saturn). Line 55 (Suspected Mods) points at Radium's BrainMixin, but that's only a guess. Entity type is on line 216. Fix: back up, remove that villager (or set removeErroringEntities=true), then test without Radium and Liberty's Villagers.

summary: The server froze for 60 seconds while saving a player's data file as they logged out, so the watchdog shut it down; the log doesn't show why the file was so slow to save.
root_quote: java.lang.Error: ServerHangWatchdog detected that a single server tick took 60.00 seconds (should be max 0.05)
note: Read the stack from the bottom up: a player disconnects, then PlayerList saves their data (PlayerDataStorage), then GZIP compression is still running when 60 seconds run out. That points to a huge player data file, but not which mod made it huge. The poster said max-tick-time=-1 stopped the crash but kicked everyone, and the only reply blamed a villager mod without proof.

summary: The server was started with Java 21, but this Minecraft version needs Java 25 (class file version 69 = Java 25).
root_quote: Caused by: java.lang.UnsupportedClassVersionError: net/minecraft/bundler/Main has been compiled by a more recent version of the Java Runtime (class file version 69.0), this version of the Java Runtime only recognizes class file versions up to 65.0
note: Fix from the thread (AMP panel): switch the Java setting to 21, start once, then switch back to 25 so Java 25 really applies. In general: install Java 25 and start the server with it.
